newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SEES TOBACCO OUTPUT DOUBLING IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SEES TOBACCO OUTPUT DOUBLING IN 1997.

text.p: Bulgaria'a agriculture ministry said on Tuesday it expected tobacco output to double to some 81,000 tonnes in 1997, compared to 39,790 tonnes in 1996 and a record low output of 25,000 tonnes in 1995.

Valya Penkova, an expert on tobacco at the ministry, said the figure was realistic and she expected the target would be met as in the present economic crisis, growing tobacco was the only way many people could make a living.

"Despite the unfavourable weather conditions in March and April, I think this output could be reached, as tobacco-growing is now the only way to make a living for many people in the country's traditional tobacco-growing areas," she told Reuters.

Penkova said the purchasing prices of tobacco would be updated in line with the official inflation index twice a year -- in mid-July and mid-October -- in order to create incentives to stimulate private tobacco growers.
Under a cabinet decision from last year producers also qualify for additional payments from the State Tobacco Fund.

Seven years ago, when tobacco output was between 100,000 and 150,000 tonnes annualy, the small Balkan country exported some 40,000 tonnes of tobacco to the former Soviet Union and only some 10,000 to western buyers.

Since the collapse of Communist trade links at the end of the 1980s, Bulgaria's tobacco exports have started going mainly to French, German and American companies. -- Galina Sabeva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
